headline: GOLD SLIPS TO $4,100 AS DECEMBER FED HIKE ODDS HIT 86% — WARSH'S HAWKISH LANGUAGE REPRICES PRECIOUS METALS
snippet: Gold slipped below $4,100 on June 23 as CME FedWatch data showed traders pricing an 86.1% probability of a December Fed rate hike — up sharply from 61% before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's June 17 FOMC meeting — with Deutsche Bank and BofA now both formally forecasting a September increase. Warsh's explicit characterisation of the US as having 'an inflation problem that's well above target and going the wrong way' has replaced geopolitical risk premium as the dominant gold pricing variable, leaving Thursday's May Core PCE release (due June 25) as the single near-term circuit-breaker for junior gold miners' share prices.

headline: LITHIUM SHEDS 14% IN ONE MONTH — CATL JIANXIAWO MINE RESTART TALK DRAGS CARBONATE TO 10-WEEK LOW AT 157,500 CNY/T
snippet: Lithium carbonate in China fell to 157,500 CNY per tonne on June 24 — down 0.63% on the day and 14% over the past month to a 10-week low — as speculation that CATL's Jianxiawo mine in Jiangxi province could resume operations weighed on near-term sentiment, though analysts cautioned the market has largely priced in a restart already. Despite the monthly decline, the price remains 161.6% above year-ago levels and new battery capacity additions expected in Q3 are forecast to maintain structural demand support; for TSX-V and ASX lithium developers, the widening gap between the spot price pullback and the year-over-year surge underscores the difference between near-term noise and the multi-year demand trajectory from EVs and energy storage.

headline: CHINA BLACKLISTS MP MATERIALS AND USA RARE EARTH — BEIJING TARGETS AMERICA'S OWN RARE EARTH CHAMPIONS
snippet: China's Ministry of Commerce added MP Materials (NYSE: MP) and USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) — the two companies most central to the US domestic rare earth independence effort — to its export control list on June 22, along with eight other US firms, citing Washington's expansion of its Chinese military-linked entity list; the restrictions bar Chinese suppliers from shipping dual-use goods to the named firms and prohibit any third party globally from passing Chinese-origin dual-use items to them. The move is largely symbolic given both companies have already worked to reduce Chinese equipment exposure, but it signals that Beijing is willing to directly target Pentagon-backed rare earth developers — MP has the DoD as a ~15% shareholder and USAR recently secured a $1.3B Department of Commerce loan agreement — as leverage in the broader critical minerals trade dispute.

headline: USA RARE EARTH REBUTS MP MATERIALS MAGNET TECH LAWSUIT — TWO US RARE EARTH GIANTS FIGHT EACH OTHER AS CHINA BLACKLISTS BOTH
snippet: On the same day China added both companies to its export control list, USA Rare Earth Inc. formally rebutted MP Materials Corp.'s lawsuit alleging that a former MP employee transferred confidential neodymium-iron-boron magnet manufacturing technology to USAR — calling the suit 'an attempt to hinder its growth' rather than a legitimate IP claim. The simultaneous China blacklisting and domestic trade secrets war underscores that the US rare earth sector's path to self-sufficiency runs through both geopolitical confrontation with Beijing and bitter corporate rivalry between the very companies Washington has funded to build the alternative supply chain.

headline: GOLDSEEK SWOT: CHINA SWALLOWED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR DEEPENS AS PRICE HITS 6-MONTH LOW
snippet: U.S. Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT published June 22 documents the structural contradiction defining the silver market in mid-2026: China imported over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026 driven by solar panel production and EV battery manufacturing, the Silver Institute projects the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit at 46.3 million ounces (the largest on record), yet silver is simultaneously testing six-month price lows near $61/oz as Federal Reserve rate-hike pricing overwhelms physical demand fundamentals. The SWOT analysis flags this divergence as the same setup that preceded silver's surge from $30 to $121 in 2024–2025 — structural deficit compression masked by institutional selling before a sharp re-rating.

headline: ALAMOS OPENS NEW 200×300m HIGH-GRADE ZONE AT ISLAND GOLD — 67.93 g/t AT CLINE-PICK AND 14.51 g/t ISLAND WEST IN SAME DRILL ROUND
snippet: Alamos Gold Inc. announced June 22 that its $43 million, 114,000-metre 2026 Island Gold District drill campaign has opened a new high-grade zone entirely outside current Mineral Resources — the Island Gold West Extension, defined over 200 x 300 metres and open to the west and down-plunge, with intercepts of 12.05 g/t Au over 5.20m and 8.07 g/t over 5.60m — while simultaneously hitting 14.51 g/t Au over 5.2m at the Island West up-plunge from 460m depth and 67.93 g/t Au over 3.05m plus 5.06 g/t over 13.60m at the Cline-Pick and Edwards regional targets seven kilometres from the Magino mill. The multi-zone simultaneous expansion signals that the Island Gold District footprint is materially larger than the current resource model captures and adds near-term mill feed optionality to Alamos's recently expanded Magino processing infrastructure.

headline: FARADAY COPPER FINDS NEAR-SURFACE COPPER AT AMERICAN EAGLE — 35m AT 0.58% Cu IN PREVIOUSLY UNEXPLORED ARIZONA ZONE
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX:FDY)
snippet: Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX:FDY) reported June 24 that its Phase IV drill program at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona intersected near-surface copper mineralisation in the previously undrilled American Eagle area: hole FCD-26-171 returned 35.35 metres at 0.58% copper from 85.40m (within 71.00m at 0.41% Cu from 80.00m) and hole FCD-26-169 hit 67.00m at 0.30% copper from 30.00m — confirming that meaningful copper grades exist in a shallow, accessible portion of the property beyond the known resource footprint. With Arizona now the subject of a June 30 Section 232 copper tariff ruling that could mandate preferential US domestic production, near-surface copper discoveries in the state carry regulatory and strategic timing that foreign porphyry projects cannot match.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS SLASHES GOLD TARGET TO $4,900 — FIRST RATE CUT NOW JUNE 2027, DOWNSIDE RISK TO $4,400 IF WARSH HIKES
snippet: Goldman Sachs cut its 2026 year-end gold price target from $5,400 to $4,900 per ounce on June 21, citing the Fed's first rate cut being pushed from December 2026 to June 2027 and markets now pricing two potential hikes rather than a single delayed cut — a structural shift that removes the 'Fed pivot premium' that drove gold from $2,000 to $5,589. Goldman flagged a downside scenario to $4,400 if Fed Chair Warsh follows through on aggressive rate increases to combat 4.2% inflation, while JPMorgan and Wells Fargo are holding $6,000 targets — creating the widest analyst divergence on gold in the current bull cycle and presenting retail investors with two radically different risk/reward maps for junior gold miners in H2 2026.

headline: URANIUM STALLS AT $85/LB — UTILITIES SHIFT FROM SPOT TO LONG-TERM CONTRACTS AS SPROTT QUIETLY BUYS 5M+ POUNDS IN 2026
snippet: Uranium spot prices held flat at $85.85 per pound as of June 23, maintaining a narrow range since April as utilities increasingly bypass the spot market in favour of long-term supply contracts — a structural shift that reduces price volatility but also reflects growing conviction that the supply deficit is durable enough to warrant multi-year commitments at current prices. The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust has purchased over 5 million pounds in 2026 year-to-date as institutional buying absorbs available spot supply, while underlying demand fundamentals — AI data centre power requirements, energy security mandates in Europe and Japan, and net-zero reactor build programmes — continue to outpace any credible near-term primary supply additions.

headline: BULLIONVAULT: WARSH'S "INFLATION GOING THE WRONG WAY" IS THE TRADE NOW — WHY GOLD CAN'T RALLY EVEN WITH IRAN RISK ON
snippet: BullionVault's June 23 analysis argues that Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's explicit characterisation of a US 'inflation problem that's well above target and going the wrong way' has fundamentally replaced geopolitical risk as the dominant gold pricing variable — meaning gold's failure to hold gains on Iran ceasefire collapse, de-dollarisation headlines, and central bank buying of 650+ tonnes isn't a sign of weakness, it's a sign that institutional traders are exclusively focused on rate-policy repricing. The piece identifies the critical trade insight: the 'buy the Fed pivot' thesis that drove gold from $2,000 to $5,589 is now in full reversal, and gold won't sustainably re-rate until either Core PCE prints convincingly below 3.4% or labour market data breaks — making Thursday's May PCE the only near-term data point that matters.
